subject: pathology
title: Signet Ring Cells, Linitis Plastica, Krukenberg Tumours, GIST, and CD117

steps.tx: Signet ring cells push nuclei aside with intracytoplasmic mucin vacuoles, growing singly without glands in diffuse gastric cancer that thickens wall into leather bottle rigidity. The mucin signet is the **signet ring cell of diffuse gastric carcinoma**. This point is tested repeatedly because it changes everyday bedside decisions.
steps.say: Mucin pushing nuclei into signets means diffuse gastric cancer infiltrating cell by lonely cell.

steps.tx: Linitis plastica stiffens the whole stomach into a nondistending leather bottle from submucosal diffuse infiltration, baffling superficial biopsies that sample only normal mucosa above tumour. Deep bites diagnose **linitis plastica, diffuse infiltrative gastric cancer**. Examiners return to it because it separates careful clinicians from guesswork.
steps.say: A stomach that will not distend with negative surface biopsies still means linitis plastica; bite deeper.

steps.tx: Krukenberg tumours return here as gastric signet ring metastases filling both ovaries, reminding that ovarian masses may be messengers whose primary hides in a stiff stomach. The metastatic messenger remains the **Krukenberg tumour of gastric signet ring origin**. Bedside recognition of this pattern saves time, blood, and unnecessary investigation.
steps.say: Bilateral solid ovarian signet tumours demand a gastric primary hunt, however quiet the stomach feels.

steps.tx: Hereditary diffuse gastric cancer from CDH1 mutation justifies genetic counselling, endoscopic surveillance with extensive random biopsies, and discussion of prophylactic total gastrectomy in confirmed carriers. That prevention dilemma is **CDH1 hereditary diffuse gastric cancer management**. Students should anchor this fact before moving to rarer causes and exceptions.
steps.say: CDH1 carriers discuss prophylactic gastrectomy because surveillance biopsies sample a haystack blindly.

steps.tx: Gastrointestinal stromal tumours arise from interstitial cells of Cajal, spindle or epithelioid, expressing KIT CD117 and DOG1, risk graded by size, mitotic rate, and site rather than benign malignant labels. The Cajal cell tumour is **gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST)**. In practice this distinction decides the next test, treatment, or referral made.
steps.say: CD117 and DOG1 positive spindle tumours of gut wall are GISTs; size and mitoses grade their danger.

vis.caption: Gastric wall anatomy framing submucosal tumours including GIST.

steps.tx: Imatinib blocking mutant KIT transformed GIST from surgery only disease into targeted therapy prototype, resistance mutations guiding sunitinib and later lines by genotype. That targeted story is **KIT inhibition by imatinib in GIST**. That is why this detail earns its place in every examination and ward round.
steps.say: Imatinib made GIST the poster child of targeted therapy; mutation type still predicts its success.

steps.tx: GISTs must not be biopsied carelessly through mucosa when resectable, because rupture and seeding convert curable tumours into peritoneal disease, so endoscopic ultrasound characterisation precedes decisions. That caution is **GIST rupture avoidance in diagnosis and surgery**. Remembering it prevents the commonest errors made with this presentation entirely.
steps.say: Never rupture a GIST; its capsule is its prognosis, in biopsy planning and surgery alike.

steps.tx: Submucosal gastric masses triage among GIST, leiomyoma, schwannoma, ectopic pancreas, and lipoma by endoscopic ultrasound layer and echogenicity before tissue strategy. Layer literacy performs **endoscopic ultrasound triage of submucosal gastric lesions**. The clinical payoff comes from applying it early, before complications accumulate further.
steps.say: Name the wall layer first in submucosal masses; ultrasound anatomy halves the differential instantly.
